title: Causal, bidirectional control of neuroimmune circuits

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a causal understanding of how defined neural pathways detect immune activity and regulate immune responses, coupled to interventions that can selectively control those pathways. Bidirectional means establishing both immune-to-neural sensing and neural-to-immune regulation. A successful system would connect an interpretable neural readout to a particular immune state and predict which intervention changes which immune function, in a specified tissue and clinical setting.

The supplied rheumatoid arthritis trial provides a clinical foundation for the regulatory direction: implanted electrical stimulation of the vagus nerve was used to engage an inflammatory reflex and modulate immune activity. The broader innovation would require substantially more than a beneficial response to stimulation. It would establish the relevant causal pathways, validate immune-sensing readouts and show that interventions produce predictable immune effects with acceptable safety.

significance.text: As a conditional scientific advance, validated circuit maps and selective interventions could make neural pathways a practical route for measuring and adjusting particular immune responses. Their value would lie in connecting a measured state, a defined intervention and a predictable immune consequence. The supplied RA trial supports the clinical plausibility of neural immune modulation in patients with inadequate response or intolerance to certain drug therapies; it does not establish the broader sensing-and-control capability.

A proposed downstream possibility is feedback-guided treatment: a validated neural signal could help determine when and how strongly to intervene, while immune measurements confirm the effect. Such a system would depend on sensing specificity, reliable causal models and evidence that feedback improves outcomes. Neither an informative neural signal nor a stimulation response alone would demonstrate this capability.

The impact would remain bounded by disease mechanisms, tissue context and the immune functions a circuit can influence. Mapping a circuit would not itself establish a cure for ME/CFS, long COVID, depression or another complex condition. Benefits in additional diseases would require their own mechanistic evidence and clinical trials. The revolutionary claim is therefore a new capacity for selective immune measurement and regulation, with applications to be demonstrated individually.

missing_breakthrough.text: The central proposed breakthrough is to move from demonstrating a clinical effect of neural stimulation to explaining and predicting the causal sequence that produces it. This requires identifying the relevant sensory and regulatory pathways, distinguishing the two directions of communication and showing which immune functions each pathway controls. The supplied evidence does not establish a general account of how signals are distributed across organs or timescales; these are dimensions that a broader research program would need to characterize.

Mechanistic uncertainty persists even within the supplied clinical example. In discussing proposed pathways for bone protection, the RA paper states that biologically plausible mechanisms require targeted confirmation in RA patients. That is a specific gap between a proposed mechanism and its validation in patients. It should not be expanded into a claim that every mechanism underlying the intervention is unknown, or treated as proof that the observed clinical benefit is false.

Proposed engineering barriers include developing neural readouts that reliably identify the immune state of interest, delivering interventions with sufficient pathway selectivity, and separating intended immune effects from other physiological consequences. Validation would also need to establish how dosing, timing and patient variation affect the response. These are requirements inferred from the proposed capability, rather than achievements or an exhaustive barrier list established by the supplied trial.

current_state.text: Tesser and colleagues’ “Vagus nerve-mediated neuroimmune modulation for rheumatoid arthritis: a pivotal randomized controlled trial,” DOI 10.1038/s41591-025-04114-7, was published online on 22 December 2025. It evaluated implanted vagus-nerve stimulation in a double-blind, randomized, sham-controlled trial involving 242 patients with moderately-to-severely active RA and inadequate response or intolerance to biological or targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. The authors classified 43% of the cohort as having difficult-to-treat RA; that classification did not apply to all 242 participants.

The trial met its primary endpoint at three months. ACR20 response occurred in 35.2% of patients receiving stimulation and 24.2% receiving sham. The reported adjusted difference was 11.8 percentage points, with a prespecified one-sided P = 0.0209. The adjusted estimate should be distinguished from the simple subtraction of the two reported response percentages. These findings establish a controlled clinical efficacy result for the studied intervention and population, rather than a general demonstration of bidirectional neuroimmune control.

Subsequent follow-up continued through 12 months, but it was open-label and permitted adjunctive therapy. Consequently, the later observations do not provide the same sham-controlled evidence as the three-month primary comparison and cannot, by themselves, isolate the longer-term contribution of stimulation. The supplied review does not provide detailed numerical safety outcomes or establish a validated immune-sensing system, a complete circuit map or broad efficacy across diseases.

The evidence available for this record is limited to the supplied review of this single published RA article. Its retained extraction was partial: PDF pages 15–18 lacked extractable text, and some graphical material was uninspected. The review nevertheless located the textual statements needed to establish trial identity, population, primary outcome and follow-up design. Those extraction limits constrain interpretation of material outside the inspected text; they do not negate the documented trial result.

Evidence-scope limitation: the supplied review contains no bounded freshness search. It therefore does not establish whether this article was the latest result, or whether the full research challenge remained open, at its stated 1 November 2026 reference date. This record preserves the documented December 2025 finding without claiming an exhaustive account of subsequent progress.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: map defined pathways in relevant tissues and use selective perturbations to establish both immune-to-neural sensing and neural-to-immune regulation. Sensing should be validated against the immune activity it is intended to represent. Regulatory experiments should test whether targeting the identified pathway produces the predicted immune change, with controls that distinguish the proposed causal pathway from alternative explanations.
completion_criteria.label: Neural pathway perturbations establish immune sensing and predicted immune regulation

completion_criteria.text: Proposed clinical demonstration: conduct controlled human studies in more than one setting, showing meaningful benefit from intervention targeting a defined circuit. Specify the required selectivity, reproducibility, clinical benefit, safety measures and follow-up duration in advance for each setting. Mechanistic studies should connect pathway engagement to immune changes and clinical outcomes, while the study design accounts for adjunctive treatment. These are proposed completion criteria, not standards established by the RA paper.
completion_criteria.label: Controlled human studies demonstrate meaningful circuit-targeted benefit in multiple settings

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility and practical boundaries: independent teams should reproduce the relevant sensing and regulatory effects, and report where performance varies across patients, tissues, disease states and intervention schedules. Durability, adverse effects and the practical burden of implantation or repeated treatment should be assessed for the intended use. Success across a finite set of studies would establish demonstrated breadth within those boundaries, not literal universality across neuroimmune circuits or diseases.
completion_criteria.label: Independent teams reproduce neuroimmune effects and report practical boundaries

related_concepts.text: Conceptual comparison with IMM-02, “A predictive, causal theory of whole immune responses”: neuroimmune circuits could supply one set of causal inputs to a broader immune-response theory. IMM-14 focuses on neural sensing and regulation; IMM-02 would need to account for additional determinants of whole immune responses. IMM-13, “Predictive causal control of microbiome–immune interactions,” similarly concerns causal communication with immunity, but through microbiome interactions. Neither concept can substitute for validating the other’s mechanisms.

Conceptual comparison with IMM-10, “Real-time immune control of life-threatening systemic inflammation”: neuroimmune interventions could become one possible control mechanism if sensing, response speed and clinical efficacy were demonstrated in that setting. IMM-10 is defined by an urgent clinical control problem, whereas IMM-14 is defined by a communication pathway and includes applications beyond acute systemic inflammation.

Conceptual comparison with IMM-04, “Durable, antigen-specific reversal of established autoimmunity,” and IMM-11, “Causal mechanisms that initiate the breakdown of self-tolerance”: improvement in RA after neural stimulation does not establish antigen-specific restoration of tolerance or explain what initially broke tolerance. IMM-05, “Routine donor-specific transplant tolerance without lifelong immunosuppression,” likewise requires donor-specific tolerance and treatment independence beyond a demonstration of immune modulation.

Conceptual comparison with IMM-09, “In-body programming of immune cells as an inexpensive, scalable treatment,” and IMM-12, “Programmable trained immunity with predictable protection and safety”: these concepts concern different means of altering immune behavior. Neural control would act through defined neuroimmune pathways, while in-body programming and trained immunity require their own evidence for the intended cellular changes, persistence and safety. IMM-08, “Restoration of youthful immune competence in older adults,” specifies a broader functional outcome that would require direct demonstration even if neural modulation contributed.

Conceptual comparison with IMM-01, “A general decoder for T-cell antigen recognition,” and IMM-03, “Vaccine design that reliably directs broadly protective antibody evolution”: identifying or regulating a neural immune pathway does not establish antigen-recognition rules or control antibody evolution. IMM-06, “General immune eradication of heterogeneous solid tumors,” and IMM-07, “Immune-mediated, treatment-free control of established HIV infection,” specify demanding disease outcomes. Neuroimmune control could be investigated as a contributor, but neither tumor eradication nor treatment-free HIV control follows from the supplied RA evidence.

Disciplinary overlap includes immunology, neuroscience, bioelectronic medicine and clinical device engineering. Device improvements may enable more precise experiments and treatment, but improved stimulation hardware alone would not complete IMM-14 without causal evidence for immune sensing and regulation.

change_log.reason: The review found that the original wording incorrectly applied the difficult-to-treat classification to the entire cohort.

change_log.reason: These quantities make the controlled result assessable and distinguish the adjusted estimate from the unadjusted difference in reported percentages.

change_log.change: Separated the sham-controlled primary comparison from open-label follow-up through 12 months.
change_log.reason: Adjunctive therapy and the later study design limit attribution of longer-term outcomes to stimulation.

change_log.change: Reframed broad statements about organs, timescales and predictive selectivity as research dimensions and proposed requirements.
change_log.reason: The single supplied article does not establish those general premises or the current status of the entire challenge.

change_log.change: Preserved the specific need for patient-level confirmation of proposed bone-protection mechanisms.
change_log.reason: The review supports this targeted mechanistic uncertainty, without establishing that every mechanism is unknown.

change_log.change: Integrated operational completion proposals, disease-specific limits, roster distinctions and evidence-access limitations.
change_log.reason: These additions preserve the review’s scientific reasoning while keeping hypothetical capabilities separate from demonstrated clinical findings.

unresolved_issues: The supplied evidence does not establish a general bidirectional circuit map, validated immune-sensing readouts or predictable selective control across tissues and diseases.
Targeted confirmation in RA patients remains necessary for the proposed bone-protection mechanisms identified in the review.
The supplied review does not provide enough safety detail or controlled longer-term evidence to characterize the intervention’s full durability and benefit–risk profile.
Pages 15–18 lacked extractable text and some graphical material was uninspected; conclusions requiring those materials cannot be resolved from the supplied review.
No freshness search was supplied, so the latest state of the field and continued openness of the full challenge are unassessed.
Operational thresholds for circuit selectivity, reproducibility, clinical benefit and follow-up remain to be specified for each proposed demonstration.

brief.title: Reading and adjusting immunity through nerves
possible: People with inflammatory disease could receive treatment guided by nerve signals that reveal what their immune system is doing. Doctors could target a defined nerve pathway to change a particular immune response predictably.
Treatment could respond as the immune state changes. A nerve signal could help determine when and how strongly to intervene, while immune measurements confirm the effect.
why: This would give doctors a way to connect an immune measurement to a treatment with a predictable effect. For patients whose medicines have failed or caused intolerable side effects, nerve stimulation could offer another route to controlling inflammation.

sources.who: John R. P. Tesser and colleagues
sources.showed: An implanted device stimulated the vagus nerve, which links the brain and body. Patients with rheumatoid arthritis who had not benefited from certain medicines improved more often with stimulation than with inactive stimulation.
sources.quote: Adverse events occurred in a similar proportion of patients in both arms.
sources.cited_for: The trial demonstrates a controlled clinical benefit from nerve stimulation in rheumatoid arthritis.
sources.not_established: It does not establish immune sensing through nerves or predictable control of particular immune functions.

sources.showed: In mice, distinct nerve cells detected cytokines, the immune system’s messenger proteins. Silencing a body–brain pathway let inflammation run unchecked; activating it suppressed inflammatory responses.
sources.quote: Genetic silencing of this body–brain circuit produced unregulated and out-of-control inflammatory responses.
sources.cited_for: The experiments connect immune sensing to a brain pathway that regulates inflammation.
sources.not_established: The mouse results do not establish a system for measuring and controlling immune responses in patients.

sources.showed: In mice, vagus nerve cells responded differently to particular cytokines. In male mice with induced bowel inflammation, background nerve activity rose while responses to specific cytokines weakened.
sources.quote: Some neurons respond selectively to individual cytokines, while others encode multiple cytokines with distinct activity patterns.
sources.cited_for: Nerve activity can distinguish immune messengers, but inflammation changes those responses.
sources.not_established: These responses do not yet provide a reliable immune measurement for guiding treatment in people.

sources.showed: In mice, stimulating vagus fibres carrying signals toward or away from the brain reduced inflammation through different mechanisms.
sources.quote: Together these results provide strong evidence for at least two discrete neuroimmune circuits that serve to downregulate immune cell function, each using divergent mechanisms of control.
sources.cited_for: The direction of nerve stimulation matters because different pathways can produce similar immune effects.
sources.not_established: The experiments do not establish selective, predictable treatment through these pathways in humans.

sources.showed: A small trial tested vagus nerve stimulation through ear skin, called ta-VNS, in young people with inflammatory bowel disease. Symptoms and a stool marker of inflammation improved; later treatment had no inactive comparison.
sources.quote: Noninvasive ta-VNS attenuated signs and symptoms in a pediatric cohort with mild to moderate inflammatory bowel disease.
sources.cited_for: The trial provides preliminary human evidence in another inflammatory disease.
sources.not_established: It does not establish lasting controlled benefit or connect a defined pathway to the clinical improvements.

shown: Mouse studies have connected immune sensing to nerve pathways that change inflammation. Tesser and colleagues have also demonstrated a clinical benefit in rheumatoid arthritis: implanted stimulation outperformed inactive stimulation during a blinded comparison.
missing: Defined pathways still need to connect reliable immune sensing with predicted immune changes in the intended tissues.
Human studies must connect selective pathway activation to immune changes and meaningful clinical benefit across settings.
A treatment system still needs to show that using nerve signals to guide stimulation improves outcomes.
Independent studies must establish durability, adverse effects and the practical burden of treatment.

milestones.label: Defined nerve pathways sense and predictably change immunity
milestones.explanation: Selective experiments would have to establish immune sensing and predicted immune changes through mapped pathways, ruling out alternatives. This would connect a readable signal to a causal means of control.

milestones.label: Controlled human studies show benefit across settings
milestones.explanation: Controlled studies in multiple settings would have to link defined pathway engagement to immune changes and meaningful benefit under preset safety and follow-up criteria. This would establish clinical usefulness.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce effects and establish practical limits
milestones.explanation: Independent teams would have to reproduce sensing and regulation while measuring variation, durability, adverse effects and treatment burden. This would establish where the approach works reliably.

uncertain: It remains unclear how reliably nerve signals identify immune states as disease changes.
Longer-term rheumatoid arthritis follow-up allowed additional medicines, leaving stimulation’s lasting contribution uncertain.
The required levels of pathway selectivity, reproducibility, clinical benefit and follow-up remain to be defined for each use.

page.title: Closed-loop neuroimmune modulation
page.definition: A system measures immune state and automatically adjusts stimulation of a defined neural circuit in people. The circuit’s immune-sensing and immune-regulating components are experimentally identified; closed-loop means that measured responses determine subsequent stimulation.

goal.need: In 2019, 18 million people worldwide had rheumatoid arthritis; WHO reports 13 million with severity potentially benefiting from rehabilitation. RESET-RA tested neural modulation in 242 adults with inadequate response or intolerance to advanced antirheumatic drugs. Its controlled results support stimulation efficacy, but do not establish immune sensing or automatic feedback control.

figures.caption: RESET-RA: ACR20 response after 3 months.
figures.note: The stratification-adjusted difference was 11.8 percentage points; the prespecified one-sided P value was 0.0209.

statements.quote: These efforts should culminate with in vivo demonstrations of predictable and automatic restoration of healthy physiological states in response to on-board physiological state monitoring.
statements.context: The published objective for Technical Area 1 included inflammatory disease within the programme’s scope.

statements.body: National Institutes of Health Common Fund, SPARC
statements.quote: SPARC-V will map the anatomical connectivity of the human vagus nerve and the physiological outcomes/endpoints of modulating its activity.

completion.title: An integrated neuroimmune feedback system restores immune state in a human feasibility study.
completion.criterion: A fully integrated system completes an early feasibility study in people with an inflammatory condition. On-board immune-state monitoring drives automatic neural intervention that restores the intended physiological state. ElectRx leaves quantitative performance metrics to individual proposals; it specifies no common sample size, duration, cytokine concentration or clinical-effect cutoff.
completion.set_by: DARPA, DARPA-BAA-15-06, section 1.2.1 anticipated Phase III target, combined with the published Technical Area 1 restoration objective; applied to the programme’s inflammatory-disease scope.
completion.threshold_quote: Early feasibility study of fully integrated, closed-loop neuromodulation technologies in humans.
completion.basis: ElectRx connects physiological restoration to an integrated human system. This is its published research target, rather than a consensus definition of all neuroimmune control. Early feasibility establishes the integrated capability; it does not establish efficacy across diseases or marketing authorisation.

milestones.title: A neuroimmune circuit has validated neural targets and an in vivo model linking activity to immune state.
milestones.criterion: Identify disease-relevant neural targets and biomarkers, and validate models linking circuit activity to physiological state in vivo. Jin et al., published on 1 May 2024, identified a mouse vagus–brainstem inflammatory circuit: silencing increased IL-6 and IL-1β and reduced IL-10; activation produced the opposite changes, with 6 mice per group in each experiment. These perturbations establish causal regulation in that model, without establishing the complete ElectRx modelling requirement.
milestones.set_by: DARPA, ElectRx Phase I objectives in its announcement of 5 October 2015 and DARPA-BAA-15-06, section 1.2.1.
milestones.threshold_quote: fundamental studies to map the neural circuits governing the physiology of diseases of interest to DARPA

milestones.title: A neural feedback signal represents its target immune variable across the intended conditions of use.
milestones.criterion: Establish the feedback signal’s relationship to the controlled immune variable across the intended population and physiological variability, with quantified limitations. Bu et al., published on 29 July 2024, recorded neck magnetic signals in 9 healthy adults after intravenous lipopolysaccharide; firing tracked circulating TNF-α. Huerta et al., published on 24 April 2025, found reduced neuronal cytokine responses during mouse colitis: TNF comparisons used 11 control and 10 colitis mice; IL-10 comparisons used 7 and 8. These studies do not establish sensing performance throughout a therapeutic controller’s intended use.
milestones.set_by: FDA, Technical Considerations for Medical Devices with Physiologic Closed-Loop Control Technology, section V.B(2); its general sensor criterion is applied here to neuroimmune feedback.
milestones.threshold_quote: the performance of the feedback variable should be established and limitations of the relationship quantified for the intended application

milestones.title: Vagus stimulation beats sham on RESET-RA’s 3-month ACR20 endpoint at one-sided α = 0.025.
milestones.criterion: In RESET-RA, NCT04539964, the stratified intention-to-treat comparison must show a higher ACR20 response rate with active stimulation than sham. ACR20 requires ≥20% improvement in tender and swollen 28-joint counts and ≥3 of pain, disability, patient assessment, clinician assessment and C-reactive protein. The paper published on 22 December 2025 reports that this endpoint was met. Follow-up through 12 months was open-label and permitted adjunctive drugs.
milestones.set_by: SetPoint Medical and RESET-RA investigators, registered trial protocol and prespecified analysis; this endpoint applies specifically to rheumatoid arthritis.
milestones.threshold_quote: The primary end point was 3-month American College of Rheumatology 20% (ACR20) response.

milestones.title: FDA approves a neural modulation device for a specified inflammatory-disease indication.
milestones.criterion: Obtain FDA premarket approval for the specified device and patient population. On 30 July 2025, FDA approved the SetPoint System under P240039 for adults with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis after inadequate response, loss of response or intolerance to one or more biological or targeted synthetic disease-modifying antirheumatic drugs. This authorisation concerns the specified treatment, without establishing immune-state feedback control.
milestones.set_by: FDA Center for Devices and Radiological Health, SetPoint System premarket approval P240039; the published authorisation is specific to rheumatoid arthritis.
milestones.threshold_quote: Based upon the information submitted, the PMA is approved.

milestones.title: Immune-state feedback controls neural stimulation in non-human primates or people.
milestones.criterion: Demonstrate feedback-controlled regulation of the target immune state in non-human primates or people, with validated physiological-state sensing, intended on-target responses, circuit specificity and assessment of off-target responses. ElectRx Phase II permits physician-in-the-loop feedback; full automation is not required. Its fully integrated human system is the subsequent programme target.
milestones.set_by: DARPA, DARPA-BAA-15-06, section 1.2.1, Technical Area 1 Phase II; applied to its immune-function scope.
milestones.threshold_quote: Demonstrate feedback-enabled neuromodulation in human (clinical) or non-human primate (preclinical).

not_found: Searches for human neuroimmune closed-loop studies found no published demonstration satisfying the integrated automatic immune-state control test.
No universal numerical threshold for neuroimmune sensing accuracy, circuit selectivity or duration was found in ElectRx, SPARC/VESPA or FDA’s physiological closed-loop guidance.
DARPA’s original ElectRx solicitation link was unavailable; its document text was accessible through GovTribe’s transcription.
The Neuromod Prize website could not be opened.

results.detail: The stratification-adjusted difference was 11.8 percentage points (P = 0.0209), meeting the one-sided 0.025 significance threshold. Follow-up after 3 months was open-label and permitted adjunctive drugs.

The decoder classified injection periods, not measured cytokine concentrations, and human therapeutic-use performance was not established.

results.finding: FDA approved the SetPoint System for eligible adults with rheumatoid arthritis on 30 July 2025; sample size not stated.
results.detail: The approval covers adults with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis after inadequate response, loss of response, or intolerance to specified drugs. The record does not establish immune-state feedback control.
results.quote: The SetPoint System is indicated for use in the treatment of adult patients with moderately to severely active rheumatoid arthritis (RA) who have had an inadequate response, loss of response, or intolerance to one or more biological or targeted synthetic disease modifying antirheumatic drugs (b/tsDMARDs).

results.finding: In 17 rheumatoid arthritis patients, stimulation frequency increased to four times daily for 8 patients after clinical-response assessment.
results.detail: Frequency was increased for patients without a moderate or good EULAR response, a physician-in-the-loop feedback rule. TNF production and disease activity improved during treatment, but the study does not isolate the effect of feedback-based escalation or establish circuit specificity in humans.
results.quote: In cohort I, two of seven patients received electric current pulses four times daily. In cohort II, 6/10 patients received electric current pulses four times daily.
